title: Mode-locking instability and multiple soliton formation in GaN polariton waveguide cavities
authors: O. Bahrova, V. Develay, H. Souissi, C. Brimont, L. Doyennette, B. Alloing, E. Cambril, S. Bouchoule, T. Ackemann, J. Zuniga-Perez, D. Solnyshkov, G. Malpuech, T. Guillet
abstract: We study the emergence of multi-soliton regimes in 1D ridge polariton waveguides of two different lengths. We show that by varying the position of the gain, which in out-of-equilibrium polariton systems is provided by the pumping laser and its associated excitonic reservoir, it is possible to tune the regime of soliton formation between single and multiple solitons. This soliton dynamics can be quantitatively reproduced by solving the Gross-Pitaevskii equations of the coupled exciton-photon system, which show that the soliton splitting mechanism is governed by the exciton reservoir dynamics.
summary: This paper reports on the controlled generation of multiple solitons in GaN polariton waveguide cavities by manipulating the pumping laser's position. Using coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equations, the authors demonstrate that tuning this gain position allows switching between single and multi-soliton regimes. This confirms that the exciton reservoir dynamics are key to governing the complex nonlinear soliton splitting mechanism.
main_problem: The study investigates the emergence of multi-soliton regimes and mode-locking instability within 1D ridge polariton waveguides.
main_result: By tuning the position of the pumping laser (gain region), researchers can control the soliton formation, transitioning between single and multiple asynchronous solitons. The mechanism governing this splitting is linked to the exciton reservoir dynamics.
method: The research combines experimental measurements (spectrally-resolved intensity) with numerical simulations solving coupled 1D Gross-Pitaevskii equations for photons, excitons, and the reservoir.
model_or_system: The physical system is a GaN polariton waveguide cavity exhibiting strong light-matter coupling. The dynamics are modeled by three coupled nonlinear differential equations (Gross-Pitaevskii type) describing photon ($\varphi$), exciton ($\chi$), and excitonic reservoir ($n_R$) populations.
key_observables: Soliton formation count (single vs. multiple), spectral distribution of emission intensity, Free Spectral Range (FSR), and group velocities of the solitons.
important_parameters: Pump position relative to cavity length, characteristic time scales ($	au_{Ph}, 	au_{Ex}, 	au_{Res}$), and coupling constants ($g_{	ext{Res}}$).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are well-approximated by the coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equations; the system is studied in 1D geometry.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the cavity structure, the transition from single to double/triple soliton spectra based on pump position, and time evolution of populations and spatial spectral intensity.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical platform (GaN polariton cavities), presents the governing coupled equations, details the experimental control knob (pump position), demonstrates the tuning mechanism between single and multiple solitons, and analyzes the underlying role of reservoir dynamics in soliton splitting.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems as it deals with nonlinear wave phenomena (solitons) in a semiconductor microcavity system where gain saturation and coupling to an external reservoir are crucial non-equilibrium effects. The control mechanism via pump position offers a tunable platform for studying complex many-body dynamics.
